title: Grilled Peri Peri Chicken Leg Quarters
summary: Chicken leg quarters marinated in a homemade roasted-pepper peri peri sauce boosted with white miso, then grilled over two-zone heat until charred, tender and sticky.
notes: Video: 'Perfect Peri Peri Chicken at Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-best-chicken-and-rice-peri-peri-jollof-recipes ('The Best Chicken and Rice (Peri Peri & Jollof)'). The page treats the chicken and the jollof rice as two recipes with their own servings: peri peri chicken serves 4 (prep 30 min plus an overnight marinade, active time 45 min). Marinating: use right away or overnight in the fridge; rest 5 minutes after grilling; jollof rice, plantains and salad serve 6-8. The video also calls it 'two recipes in one', so the jollof rice, plantains and salad are a separate file (jollof-rice-joshua-weissman). Prep 30 min is the page's; cook 45 min is the page's active time, which fits the video's grilling (about 5 minutes direct, 20-30 minutes indirect, 5 minutes rest), so times_basis is estimated. The video states all sauce amounts except the 1/4 cup of oil blended in at the end (captions read 'a/4 cup'; the page gives 1/4 cup). All of the sauce is counted in full (house rules 1, 3 and 10): it is made for this dish and fully used, 1 cup in the miso marinade (a thick paste rubbed under the skin, with what is left in the bowl brushed on during grilling) and the remaining ~1/4 cup drizzled on the chicken. Our estimates: Thai chilis 2 g each; bay leaves 0.25 g each (they are blended into the sauce, so they are eaten); 1/4 tsp kosher salt for 'a little salt to taste' in the pan; 1/2 tsp kosher salt for the 'touch more salt' before grilling; leg quarter weight, 340 g each as bought, bone-in (see that line). Ranges: oil 2-3 Tbsp, we use 2 (the page also says 2); lemon juice 1-2 Tbsp, we use 1. Optional xanthan gum (1/8 tsp) is not counted: he recommends it but is not clearly seen adding it (house rule 11). Not counted: the splash of water used to deglaze (no amount; no nutrition) and the oil for greasing the grill (no amount). He uses Fresno and Thai chilis in place of piri piri chilis; Fresno uses the existing fresh red chili record, Thai chilis are weighed in grams on the same record. Red onion uses USDA 'Onions, raw' as a proxy (see new_h3.csv).

A little salt, for the sauté

steps.text: Peri peri sauce: thinly slice the Thai chilis (seeds in) and the stemmed Fresnos, cut the seeded red bell pepper into rough 1-inch pieces, and roughly dice the half red onion. Keep the 10 peeled garlic cloves whole.

Heat the oil in a large stainless skillet over medium heat. Add the vegetables, a little salt and the bay leaves and sauté, stirring now and then, 4-5 minutes, until very soft with a few charred spots.
Lower the heat slightly, add the smoked paprika, dill, thyme and black pepper, and toast 30-60 seconds.
Scrape everything, bay leaves included, into a blender. Deglaze the pan with a splash of water and add that too. Add the lemon zest and juice, salt and sugar.

Blend from medium up to high until as smooth as possible, then stream in the avocado oil. For a sauce that never separates, sprinkle in the xanthan gum while blending on high. Adjust the salt and lemon, strain if you want it glossy, and cool.

Whisk 1 cup of the sauce with the miso until smooth; keep the remaining sauce (about 1/4 cup) for drizzling. Rub the marinade all over the leg quarters and under the skin. Use right away or cover and refrigerate overnight.
Set up a two-zone grill and grease the grate. Salt the chicken lightly and grill skin side down over the hot side for 2-3 minutes, flip and grill 2-3 minutes more; some char is good.
Brush both sides with the marinade left in the bowl, move to the cool side, cover and cook 20-30 minutes, until the meat reaches about 185°F (75°C).
If you like, brush with more sauce and crisp the skin briefly over the hot side. Rest 5 minutes, then serve, drizzled with the reserved sauce, with the jollof rice and sides.
